# Behavioral Specification: Flash Physical Read Pipeline

## 1. Purpose

This module implements the read path of the flash physical controller. It accepts flash read requests, optionally caches recently read flash words, fetches missing words from the flash primitive, applies reliability error correction, optional descrambling, and plaintext integrity checking, and returns read data and error status in the order the requests were accepted.

The read request interface may be back-pressured. The response interface has no back-pressure: once a response is presented, the consumer must accept it in the same cycle.

## 2. Interface Overview

The module shall operate from a single clock and an asynchronous active-low reset.

The module provides:

- A read request interface, including the read address, partition selection, information-page selection, scramble/descramble requirement, ECC enable, program/erase sideband status, buffer enable, and arbitration error indication.
- A response interface that presents read data, response-valid indication, data-error indication, reliability ECC error indication, plaintext integrity error indication, and single-bit ECC error information.
- An interface to the flash primitive for issuing fetch requests and receiving fetched data.
- An interface to the descrambling logic for mask calculation and descrambling requests.
- An idle indication and an internal FIFO/queue error indication.

## 3. Reset and Initialization

After reset:

- No read request shall be accepted.
- No flash fetch shall be outstanding.
- No read response shall be pending.
- The read buffer/cache shall be empty and disabled.
- The idle indication shall be asserted.

The buffer-enable input may change only while no read response is pending. While the buffer-enable input differs from the currently active buffer-enable state, no new read request shall be accepted. After the new value has taken effect, normal read acceptance may resume.

## 4. Read Request Acceptance and Ordering

A read request is accepted when the request is present and the module asserts request-ready in the same cycle.

Every accepted read shall be assigned a position in the response order. Responses shall be returned in the same order as the corresponding requests were accepted. A later read must not bypass an earlier read, even if the later read hits the buffer and the earlier read requires a flash fetch or descrambling.

A read that hits an already valid buffer entry or a buffer entry that is currently being filled shall be accepted without issuing a flash fetch, provided internal response resources are available.

A read that misses the buffer shall be accepted only when:

- the flash fetch stage is available to start the fetch in the same cycle,
- the flash primitive is ready to accept the fetch,
- internal storage for read data, mask data, and response-order information is available,
- no buffer dependency prevents allocation, and
- no mask calculation is currently outstanding.

While a descrambling mask calculation is outstanding, the module shall not accept any new read request, including buffer hits.

The module shall not accept a read if all buffer entries are currently depended upon by outstanding ordered responses. At least one dependency must clear before further reads may be accepted.

## 5. Read Buffer Behavior

The read buffer holds recently fetched flash-word data. Buffer entries are distinguished by flash-word address, partition, and information-page selection. A read shall hit only when all of those attributes match an existing entry.

When the buffer is disabled:

- No buffer lookup shall be used.
- No buffer entry shall be allocated.
- Every accepted read shall be issued to the flash primitive.

When the buffer is enabled:

- A valid entry may serve a later read to the same flash word.
- An entry that is currently being filled may also be matched by a later read. That later read shall wait until the entry is filled, and shall then receive its data in the appropriate response order.
- An entry that is currently being filled shall not be evicted or replaced.
- When a new entry must be allocated, an invalid entry shall be selected in preference to a valid entry.
- If no invalid entry is available, a valid entry that has no outstanding response dependency shall be selected. Selection among such entries shall be fair.
- A valid entry that has an associated error shall not be used to satisfy a new read. If a response has already been ordered to use that entry, the stored error shall be returned with that response.

## 6. Invalidation on Program and Erase

The module does not issue program or erase operations, but it shall observe sideband program and erase indications in order to prevent stale buffer data from being returned.

The following invalidation behavior shall apply:

- A program indication targeting the same flash word, partition, and information page shall invalidate any matching valid buffer entry.
- A page-erase indication shall invalidate any valid buffer entry whose page, partition, and information page match the erase address.
- A bank-erase indication shall invalidate all valid buffer entries.

These sideband operations shall be presented only while the read pipeline is idle and no read response is pending.

## 7. Flash Fetch and Reliability ECC

When a read misses the buffer, the module shall issue a fetch request to the flash primitive for the entire flash word containing the requested bus word.

Only one flash fetch shall be outstanding at a time. The module shall not issue a new fetch until the current fetch has returned its data. A buffer hit may still be accepted while a fetch is outstanding.

When fetched data returns, the module shall apply reliability ECC if and only if the transaction’s ECC-enable attribute is asserted.

If ECC is enabled:

- A detected single-bit error shall be corrected before the data is used or stored. The module shall assert the single-bit error indication and report the flash-word address of that read. The corrected data shall be returned normally and shall not cause an in-band data error.
- A detected multi-bit error shall be treated as an uncorrectable reliability error. The module shall assert an in-band data error on the corresponding response and shall also assert the out-of-band reliability ECC error indication when the raw flash read completes. The ECC-decoded word shall be used as the returned data, even though it may be unreliable.

If ECC is disabled, no reliability ECC correction or error reporting shall be applied, and the raw fetched data shall be used.

Reliability ECC shall be applied only when data is first fetched from flash. Data served later from the buffer is not re-checked for reliability ECC errors.

## 8. Erased Flash Word Handling

A fetched flash word in which all bits are one shall be treated as erased.

If the erased word was requested with the scramble/descramble attribute asserted, the module shall not descramble it. The erased data shall be treated as plain data and may be returned directly. Any mask calculation that has been started for that address shall be discarded once the mask is available.

## 9. Descrambling Behavior

For a read that requires descrambling, the module shall obtain a mask calculated from the read address. The mask calculation may begin only after the corresponding flash fetch has been accepted by the flash primitive.

The mask calculation shall use the flash-word address of the read. While the mask calculation is pending, no new read shall be accepted.

When both the fetched data and the calculated mask are available:

- If the word requires descrambling, the module shall request the descrambler to process the data.
- The data presented to the descrambler shall be the fetched data combined with the mask.
- The final returned data shall be the descrambler output combined with the same mask.
- The descramble request shall be held until the descrambler acknowledges completion.

If the word is erased, the descrambler shall not be invoked for that word.

A read that does not require descrambling shall not use the descrambler and may be returned directly once its data is available, subject to response ordering.

## 10. Response Data and Integrity

Each response shall return the requested bus word of the flash word. If a flash word contains multiple bus words, the requested word offset shall be part of the ordered response information, and the correct bus word shall be selected.

The module shall generate bus-integrity metadata for the returned data. The response shall be presented on both the host-facing data output and the controller-facing data output. Both outputs shall carry the same logical response and error status. The host-facing output shall apply the address-XOR encoding required by the host bus; the controller-facing output shall not apply that encoding.

If the transaction’s ECC-enable attribute is asserted, the module shall check the plaintext integrity tag carried with the de-scrambled data. This check shall be performed for data returned from the flash pipeline and for data returned from the buffer.

If the plaintext integrity tag does not match:

- The module shall assert the in-band data-error output for that response.
- The module shall assert the out-of-band plaintext integrity error output.

When the in-band data error is asserted for a response, the data payload returned to the consumer shall be the invalid-data pattern: all-ones data with the bus-integrity metadata recomputed for that pattern. This invalid-data pattern shall be used instead of the flash contents.

## 11. Error Reporting

The module shall distinguish the following error categories:

- Reliability ECC single-bit errors: corrected and reported out-of-band with the flash-word address.
- Reliability ECC multi-bit errors: reported out-of-band when the flash read completes and reported in-band when the corresponding response is delivered.
- Plaintext integrity errors: reported out-of-band and in-band when the corresponding response is delivered.
- Stored buffer errors: if a response is ordered to use a buffer entry that has a recorded reliability error, the response shall assert the in-band data-error output.
- Catastrophic arbitration errors: if asserted, the module shall force the in-band data-error output and the invalid-data output pattern. This shall occur regardless of whether a read response is currently being presented.
- Internal queue integrity errors: if an internal response or storage queue reports an integrity failure, the module shall assert the queue error output.

## 12. Idle Indication

The idle output shall be asserted when no accepted read is awaiting response and no response is pending. After reset, the module shall be idle.

The idle indication shall be used as the safe condition for changing the buffer-enable input and for presenting program/erase sideband operations.

## 13. Response Valid Behavior

The response-valid output shall be asserted when the module has completed the next response in order. Because the response interface has no ready/back-pressure, asserting response-valid shall also consume that response from the ordered response queue in the same cycle.

The module shall be able to deliver a response for a buffer hit without waiting for any flash fetch, but shall not deliver it ahead of older responses.

# Behavioral Specification: Flash Physical Read Pipeline

## 1. Scope

This specification describes the behavior of the flash physical read pipeline module. The module is responsible for accepting flash read transactions, maintaining a small read cache, reading flash memory, performing optional reliability error checking and descrambling, and returning read data in order to the requesting path.

The module does **not** include program or erase datapath behavior. It only responds to program and erase operations as cache-maintenance events that invalidate previously read data.

---

## 2. Reset and Initial State

- After reset, the module must be idle and must not have any pending read responses.
- The read cache must be disabled after reset.
- No read request may be accepted until the module is out of reset and the cache-enable input has settled to a valid value.

---

## 3. Read Request Interface

### 3.1 Request Acceptance

- A read transaction is accepted only when the module asserts its request-ready indication.
- The module must not assert request-ready unless it has enough internal storage to complete the transaction and return exactly one response.
- The response side has no backpressure. Therefore, before accepting a request, the module must ensure that it will be able to deliver the response without stalling.

### 3.2 Cache Hit

- If a request matches a valid entry in the read cache, the module may accept it without starting a flash read.
- If a request matches an entry that is currently being filled by an in-flight flash read, the module may accept it and must wait for that fill to complete before returning data.
- A cache hit must not cause a new flash read.

### 3.3 Cache Miss

- If a request does not match any cache entry, and caching is enabled, the module must allocate a cache entry for the request.
- If caching is disabled, the module must not allocate or look up cache entries; every read must access the flash array.
- A cache-miss request is accepted only when the flash array is ready to accept the read. The module may hold request-ready deasserted until the flash read handshake has completed.

### 3.4 Response Order

- Accepted read requests must be responded to in the same order they were accepted.
- A cache hit may be accepted and become ready earlier than older misses, but it must not overtake them in the response stream.
- Every accepted read request must produce exactly one response.

---

## 4. Cache Behavior

### 4.1 Cache Enable

- The read cache is controlled by a cache-enable input.
- If the cache-enable input changes, the module must stop accepting new read requests until the new value is active.
- The new cache-enable value is applied only when the read pipeline is idle.
- When caching is disabled, no lookup occurs, no entries are allocated, and all reads access the flash array.

### 4.2 Cache Entry Matching

- A cache entry stores the flash word address, partition, and information-select attributes of the read that filled it.
- A later request hits only if all of these attributes match.
- A cache entry that is marked as having an error must not be used to satisfy a new read request unless a response for that entry is already queued.

### 4.3 Cache Entry States

A cache entry can be in one of the following states:

- **Invalid**: available for allocation.
- **Being filled**: a flash read for this entry is outstanding or is being processed but the entry does not yet contain final data.
- **Valid**: contains final read data and can satisfy future read requests.

### 4.4 Allocation and Replacement

- The module must prefer to allocate an invalid entry over replacing a valid entry.
- A valid entry may be replaced only if it is not needed by any already accepted response.
- An entry that is currently being filled must not be replaced.
- If multiple valid entries are eligible for replacement, the module must choose among them in a fair or rotating manner.
- If all usable entries are busy or depend on pending responses, the module must hold off new requests until an entry becomes available.

### 4.5 Cache Fill Error Handling

- If a flash read used to fill a cache entry detects an uncorrectable reliability error, the error must be stored with the entry.
- If a response is already queued for that entry, that response must be returned with the error indication.
- Once no queued response depends on the entry, the entry must be treated as invalid for future lookups and may be reused.

---

## 5. Flash Array Read Behavior

### 5.1 Read Issuance

- The module must issue one flash read for every accepted cache miss.
- The module must not have more than one outstanding flash read at a time.
- A new flash read may begin as soon as the previous flash read has returned data and the internal storage between the read stage and descrambling stage has capacity.

### 5.2 Read Completion

- When a flash read completes, the module must determine whether the returned word requires descrambling.
- If no descrambling is required, and there is no older data ahead in the pipeline, the response may be generated immediately.
- If descrambling is required, the read data must be held until the descrambling operation completes and the response can be emitted in order.

### 5.3 Erased Word Handling

- A flash word in which every bit is 1 is treated as erased.
- If the read address is marked as requiring descrambling but the data is all 1s, the module must not descramble the data.
- In that case, the module must wait for any associated mask calculation to complete, then discard the mask and return the all-ones data.

---

## 6. Descrambling Behavior

- For a read that is marked as requiring descrambling and is not erased, the module must request a mask calculation for the flash word address.
- The mask calculation must begin when the flash read is accepted and must proceed in parallel with the flash read itself.
- While a mask calculation is outstanding, the module must not accept another read request.
- Once the mask calculation completes, the descrambling operation may overlap with a later flash read, provided the inter-stage storage is available.
- The module must present the stored read data and the calculated mask to the descrambling logic and wait for the descrambling operation to complete before forwarding the final data.
- If descrambling is not required, no mask calculation is needed.

---

## 7. Error Detection and Reporting

### 7.1 Reliability Error Checking

- The module must check the reliability error code on data returned from the flash array only when the read is marked as having reliability error checking enabled.
- If reliability checking is disabled, no reliability error must be reported, and the raw flash word must be passed through.

#### Single-Bit Reliability Error

- If reliability checking is enabled and a single-bit error is detected, the module must correct the error before storing or returning the data.
- The corrected data must be used for the cache entry and for the response.
- The module must assert a single-bit error status indication and provide the flash word address associated with the error.

#### Multi-Bit Reliability Error

- If reliability checking is enabled and a multi-bit error is detected, the module must assert a multi-bit reliability error indication.
- The multi-bit error must also cause the eventual read response to be flagged as an in-band error.
- The data returned for a multi-bit error is the error-correcting-code output, which may not be the original data.

### 7.2 Integrity Tag Checking

- The flash word contains an integrity tag that is checked after descrambling.
- If a read is marked as having integrity checking enabled, the module must recompute the integrity tag over the selected data and compare it with the stored tag.
- If the tags do not match, the module must:
  - assert an in-band error on the response, and
  - assert an out-of-band integrity error indication.
- This check must be performed for both flash array reads and cache hits.

### 7.3 Error Responses

- When a response is flagged as an error, the data payload presented to the controller-side output must be an all-ones pattern with the correct integrity encoding, rather than the actual read data.
- The host-side output applies the normal host-side address transform to this error pattern.

### 7.4 Catastrophic Arbitration Error

- If the module receives a catastrophic arbitration error indication, it must propagate this as an in-band read error indication.

### 7.5 Internal FIFO Error

- If any internal FIFO detects a storage integrity failure, the module must assert a dedicated FIFO error indication.
- This is a fatal error indication and is separate from normal read-data error reporting.

---

## 8. Data Output Behavior

### 8.1 Output Data Buses

- The module provides read data on two output paths: a host-side path and a controller-side path.
- Both output paths must carry the same logical response data and integrity information.
- The host-side path must XOR the data field with the relevant address bits. The controller-side path must not apply this address transform.

### 8.2 Wide Flash Words

- If a flash word is wider than one bus word, the module must cache the entire flash word.
- When responding, the module must return only the bus word selected by the read address.
- The selected bus word must carry the correct bus integrity encoding.

### 8.3 Response Valid

- The module must present each response as a single-cycle valid indication.
- The response consumer is expected to accept the response in that cycle; the module does not wait for a response-ready signal.

---

## 9. Idle Behavior

- The module must assert its idle indication when there are no accepted read requests waiting to be responded to.
- Idle is used to qualify cache-enable changes and program/erase cache-maintenance operations.
- When idle is asserted, the read pipeline has no pending responses.

---

## 10. Program and Erase Cache Maintenance

- The module must observe program, page-erase, and bank-erase indications for cache coherence purposes.

### 10.1 Program

- A program operation must invalidate any valid cache entry whose flash word address, partition, and information-select match the program address.

### 10.2 Page Erase

- A page erase operation must invalidate any valid cache entry that falls in the same flash page, partition, and information-select as the erased page.

### 10.3 Bank Erase

- A bank erase operation must invalidate all valid cache entries in the affected bank.

### 10.4 Work-in-Progress Entries

- A cache entry that is currently being filled must not be evicted by program or erase maintenance operations.

---

## 11. Summary of Key Requirements

- Accept read requests in order and return one response per accepted request.
- Maintain cache coherence across program, page erase, and bank erase operations.
- Preserve response ordering.
- Apply reliability error checking and descrambling only when required.
- Apply integrity checking on all appropriate responses, including cache hits.
- Provide both host-side and controller-side read data outputs with appropriate integrity encoding.
- Report single-bit reliability errors, multi-bit reliability errors, integrity errors, and internal FIFO errors on their respective status paths.
- Never accept new read requests unless the module can complete them without stalling the unbackpressured response path.
